question: Will Indiana use a new congressional map for the 2026 United States midterm elections?
thesis: Structural longshot-bias read, not live news. The Indiana Senate voted down the mid-decade congressional redistricting push in December 2025 (31-19 against), ending the only legislative path to a new map; Indiana's 2026 candidate filing closed in February and its primary was held on 5 May 2026 under the existing 2021 map. Resolution requires a map that is enacted AND in effect for the 2026 midterm -- adopting a new map after the primary has already been run on the old districts would require re-running nominations, which has no precedent and no live proposal. The only YES paths are (a) a special session reversing the Senate vote after the primary plus a court allowing a post-primary map swap, or (b) a resolver counting something other than a genuinely new enacted map. I price that residual at ~1.2%; the market's 4.5% is the usual 3-5c floor that dead tails carry on Polymarket (same family as the frozen aliens/Greenland/impeachment legs). Kill: any credible report of an Indiana special session on redistricting before 3 Nov 2026 invalidates the thesis.
